reasons: No error boundary, so any crash shows a blank page.

terms.meaning: A development-only React mode that checks for common mistakes and runs some code twice to expose them.
The first file that runs when the app loads.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Startup and drawing the app
sections.what: Finds the empty root element in the page and draws the App component into it.
sections.why: Likely reason: this is how React apps begin. StrictMode is a development aid.
sections.watch_out: The root element id here must match the one in index.html.

summary: Starts the React app and places the App component into the page's root element.
purpose: The entry point. It is the first frontend code the browser runs.
why: Standard React startup. StrictMode asks React to flag common mistakes during development.
how: Imports React, the DOM library, the App component and the styles. Finds the root element in the page and renders App inside StrictMode.
inputs: The root element from index.html, the App component and the styles.
outputs: The whole app drawn in the browser.
risks: The exclamation mark after the root lookup assumes the element exists. If it is missing, the page is blank with an error in the console. StrictMode runs some effects twice in development, so the Dashboard request runs twice there.
debug: If the page is blank, check the browser console for an error about the root element and confirm the id in index.html matches.
